description: User has a race goal (half marathon) but discloses significant injury history and explicitly says staying healthy is the priority. Dean must probe the injury history specifically — not just acknowledge and move on.

conversation_history.content: Hey! I'm Coach Dean — I'll send you a coaching note after every run you log on Strava: what it meant, whether to push or back off, and what's coming. What's your name, and what are you training for?

Maya. Training for a half marathon in October — but honestly finishing healthy is more important to me than time. I had a stress fracture two years ago that wiped out six months of running and I really can't go through that again.

inbound_message: Maya. Training for a half marathon in October — but honestly finishing healthy is more important to me than time. I had a stress fracture two years ago that wiped out six months of running and I really can't go through that again.

ground_truth.notes:
Maya has two things in this message: a race goal (half marathon, October) and a significant injury history (stress fracture, 6 months lost). In the new architecture, deep injury intake happens in a dedicated stage AFTER Strava connects — the goals stage acknowledges injury briefly and continues.

Correct behavior: Acknowledge the stress fracture history seriously without dismissing it — show it registered. Then ask the single most important next question, which is either: the specific race name/date (she said 'half marathon in October' without naming a race), or asking for Strava. E.g. 'That history matters — I'll want to understand it properly. Is there a specific race in October you're targeting?' or 'Noted on the stress fracture — that's going to shape how we approach training. Have you connected Strava yet?'

Do NOT probe the injury with detailed follow-up questions in the goals stage (e.g. 'Where was the fracture — shin, foot?'). Thorough injury intake happens in the dedicated injury stage after Strava connects.
Do NOT give generic reassurance ('we'll be careful', 'gradual progression'). Dismissal dressed as acknowledgment.
Do NOT ignore the injury and immediately jump to Strava with no acknowledgment.

The acknowledgment should feel genuine — Dean heard the stress fracture history as important context. But the goals stage job is to get name + goal + race date + Strava. The injury depth comes later.
